messages:
Sam: Heads-up — noticed a p99 jump for /v1/generate on the latency dashboard right after yesterday's routing weight tweak. p50/p95 look unchanged. Anyone else seeing this?
Maria: yep. saw the spike around 18:02UTC. seems correlated with fallback route being selected more often for a subset of tenants. kv-cache miss rate goes up and tail balloons.
Kevin: curious — the dashboard shows the endpoint rolled up as a single p99 (merged). where do we surface sample origin? UI just says 'merged' which isn't helpful.
Maria: the aggregation service is doing a t-digest merge across route origins. if a fallback route has a fat tail, the merged tdigest can move the 99th even if it had fewer raw samples. classic merge skew.
Sam: ah — that explains big part of it, but our counts showed the primary route still had most requests. I'm worried about time alignment too: console query window is event_time based, our rollup job uses ingest_time for buckets. retries and delayed logs could be in different windows and bias the merge.
Kevin: that mismatch will absolutely flip p99 in edge cases. simple repro: run the rollup with event_time vs ingest_time and compare p99. I can throw a quick query: `SELECT pctl(0.99, latency_ms) AS p99, count() FROM traces WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' BY route, origin WINDOW 1m` and then compare against rollup output.
Maria: I repro'd locally: when fallback requests have ~10% higher latency and show up slightly later (ingest delay 10-30s), the merged p99 reported on the dashboard jumps even though user-visible p95/p50 are fine.
Sam: short term: can we add provenance on the percentile tooltip? something like "merged (origins: primary=78%, fallback=22%, fallback_p99=1.45s)" so folks can see why p99 moved.
Kevin: +1. Also propose exposing sample counts per origin in the breakdown panel. plus a note in rollout UX: "percentiles are computed by merging per-origin t-digests; small-origin tails can dominate p99."
Maria: longer-term: consider changing merge heuristic — prefer sample-weighted merges or fall back to raw sample reconstruction when counts are low. we could also add a stability flag that prefers the origin with higher sample count for p99 if other origins have <N samples.
Sam: sounds good. cc @nx-deploy-bot can we create a ticket and maybe flag a canary on the routing weight change? would like to revert if the canary shows tail regressions.
nx-deploy-bot: Created INF-4321: "Investigate p99 uplift for /v1/generate after routing-weight change" assigned to @Kevin and @Maria. Canary scheduled for next rollout window. :white_check_mark:
Kevin: I'll attach the quick diff to the rollup query and draft the tooltip copy. Maria — can you run a small replay to measure how often fallback tail wins the merged p99?
Maria: on it. I'll share numbers in INF-4321 and dump a short table. expect results in ~30m.
Sam: thanks team. if we can get the dashboard to show origin counts and a one-line explanation, that should reduce pager noise while we decide on merge policy.
